tasks.task: Run a financial health check of the business

items.when: When you have the P&L, balance sheet and bank statements and need five areas rated with evidence
Before you rate anything, to find mismatches, duplicates and gaps in the books you were given
When you need the full ratio set worked out from the accounts before you judge each area
When the cash cycle looks slow and you need debtor, creditor and stock days with the cash held in each
When a few customers or one supplier carry the business and the risk needs a limit and a plan
When the totals look fine but nobody has read the cost lines closely

tasks.task: Write the monthly finance pack for the owner

items.when: When the month is closed and you need the order of work, from checks to the owner meeting
When the numbers are ready and the owner needs key figures, trends, risks and decisions in plain words
When lines moved against last month and each one needs a written reason
When the owner has a budget and wants to know what moved against it and why
When the pack has no fixed set of numbers yet and you must pick the few the owner decides on
When a figure will not land with a non-finance owner and needs a comparison they can picture
Before the pack goes out, to find accounts that do not reconcile and odd entries in the close

tasks.task: Build a cash forecast and find the tight weeks

items.when: When you have open invoices, bills and fixed costs and need a 30, 60 and 90 day cash view
When sales are seasonal and the owner needs a dated forecast, a downside case and a buffer
When a past forecast exists, to see how far it missed before anyone trusts the new one
When the forecast only works if nothing goes wrong, to see where it breaks in a bad year

tasks.task: Find cash inside the business when it is short

items.when: When cash is tight and you need six levers ranked by how much cash each frees
Before you choose a lever, to see whether debtors, stock or supplier terms hold the cash
When longer supplier terms are the lever and you need what to ask for and what it costs
When late-paying customers are the lever and someone must chase open invoices every week

tasks.task: Set the finance priorities for the next 90 days

items.when: Before you set priorities, to know which of the five areas is red and why
When cash is the red area, to see six levers ranked before you pick three priorities
When the priorities are chosen and each needs an owner, weekly check-ins and risks
When the plan is drafted, to list the ways it could fail and change it first

tasks.task: Weigh one big money decision in a short memo

items.when: When the owner faces one large choice and wants a two-page memo with options and a call
When you want two to four options side by side with cash out, return and a downside case
When the choice is a purchase and you need payback, return and risk worked out
When the choice is hiring now or later and you need base, best and worst cost cases
Before you recommend, to test how big a loss one bad year brings if the bet fails
When the owner already loves one option and the forecast behind it looks hopeful

tasks.task: Map every debt and plan the order to pay it off

items.when: When the owner juggles loans, cards and leases and needs them on one page with true cost
When you want two payoff orders compared, with the timeline and total interest of each
When several loans fall due, to check cash covers each date and find the biggest gap
When the debts cannot be met as written and each creditor needs proposed new terms

tasks.task: Explain a loan offer and what it really costs

items.when: When a lender sends an offer letter and the owner needs cost, limits and questions in plain words
When the full agreement arrives, to flag risky terms and when to bring in a lawyer
When fees and discounts come off the top, to see the cash the business really receives

tasks.task: Plan a talk with the lender when payments are tight

items.when: When a missed payment or covenant test is in sight and the owner needs a calm, factual plan
When the loan has a cash cover test and you need the headroom for each test period
Before the call, to set the opening, the questions to ask and the fallback
When the owner dreads the call and needs to start from how the lender sees it

tasks.task: Build the budget and a model with scenarios

items.when: When the owner needs next year's budget and a forecast from past numbers and plans
When a lender or buyer needs profit, balance sheet and cash models that tie together
When the budget is drafted, to score how it survives a bad year and where it breaks
Before anyone relies on the workbook, to find formula errors, broken links and tie-out fails
When the plan has no answer to a shock that could end the business

tasks.task: Check the books can be relied on before advising

items.when: When you get ledger and payment reports and need mismatches and missing receipts flagged
When gross margin looks wrong because costs sit in the wrong part of the P&L
When you get bank and ledger exports and need unreconciled accounts and odd entries listed

tasks.task: Find which products, jobs or costs drain profit

items.when: When you have revenue and costs by product and need to see which lines lose money
Before you read margin, to sort each cost line into direct cost or overhead
When overheads crept up line by line and nobody can say what each one buys

tasks.task: Rebuild reported profit into profit a buyer can rely on

items.when: When you have the accounts and need add-backs, one-offs and owner costs set out with proof
When you need the cash an owner could take out each year, shown as a range
When an add-back looks large, to test it against a documented cap
When the records do not add up and you need the money flows traced and the next checks listed
When adjusted profit keeps growing with every add-back the seller suggests

tasks.task: Write the due diligence request list for a purchase

items.when: When a buyer has a broker summary or first accounts and needs the steps before an offer
When you need the documents and answers to ask the seller for, ranked by deal impact
When the list must be split by workstream with status tracking as answers come in
When a first-time buyer has the listing and the books and wants a guided first pass
Before a seller meeting, to get sharp questions, benchmarks and red flags to probe

tasks.task: Write a red-flag report on a target's financials

items.when: Before you list red flags, to know how far reported profit differs from reliable profit
When you need red flags and valuation checks pulled into one view of the purchase
When sales lean on a few customers and the buyer needs that risk sized
When profit may depend on the owner, to find the work only the owner does

tasks.task: Estimate a value range and test the asking price

items.when: When you have the accounts and a price and need to see if the price leaves room for error
When you want cash flow, peer multiple and past deal values side by side as a range
Before an offer, to set a walk-away price and the best alternative
When the seller's growth story and the numbers behind the price do not match

tasks.task: Work out cash needed after buying and at closing

items.when: When the buyer needs the first 90 days of cash after takeover, with risks named
When new debt funds the deal, to check the cash it raises covers payoff and closing
When the price has a working capital target and the true-up after closing must be worked out
When a seller asks what they will receive at closing after debt and costs

tasks.task: Score how ready the business is to sell and plan the fixes

items.when: When an owner plans to sell and needs seven areas scored with the evidence behind each
When the sale is one to three years away and the fixes need a month-by-month programme
When the owner's role scores low and each task needs a deputy and a handover note
When key roles have no cover and a buyer will ask who runs the business next
When the customer area scores low, to set limits and a plan a buyer can believe

tasks.task: Build the document index for the buyer's checks

items.when: When the files exist and you need a versioned index and a map of what requests they cover
Before indexing, to know what a buyer in this sector will ask for
When the index is drafted, to check each scored area has its evidence filed

tasks.task: Write a one-page business profile for a broker

items.when: When the business must not be named yet and buyers need a one-page reason to ask for more
When the broker wants a named one-page sheet with financials, ratios and a summary
When interest is real and the broker needs the longer sale document drafted
Before it goes out, to find where the profile contradicts what staff or lenders were told

tasks.task: Check where cash sits and the money risks around it

items.when: When a large balance sits at one bank and you need how much is above protection limits
When the business holds debt or foreign currency and needs a liquidity and rate plan
When the owner wants every money risk listed, sized and stress tested

tasks.task: Prepare a board, investor or lender update

items.when: When decisions are due and the board needs an evidence map and a clear update
When the update is a deck and the story, numbers and bad news need placing
When the update is drafted, to face the toughest questions before the room asks them
When lender, board and staff each hear a different version of the numbers

tasks.task: Prepare questions for the tax adviser or lawyer

items.when: When one decision has tax effects and the owner needs facts, options and questions for a tax pro
When the structure may be wrong and you need options compared on risk, tax and paperwork
When a contract drives the decision and the lawyer needs the risky terms listed first

always.when: Before any advice built on the books, to know whether the numbers can be trusted
Before any workbook leaves, to catch formula errors, broken links and totals that do not tie
Before the owner reads it, to find finance jargon and put it in plain words

helpers.when: When the books are not closed or reconciled and must be fixed before any review
When the job needs job costing, stock valuation or a full monthly management accounts pack
When the job needs a detailed driver-based budget, forecast or scenario model built
When freeing cash depends on chasing customers or resetting supplier payment runs
When thin margin is a pricing problem and prices or discounts must be reset
When the answer to the cash gap is raising equity from investors

gaps: No library item builds a 13-week direct cash forecast by week; the cash forecast item works in 30, 60 and 90 day blocks
No library item writes a monthly management pack for an owner-led business; only the kit prompt covers it
No library item compares lease, hire purchase and outright purchase for equipment, vehicles or property
No library item works out the true yearly cost of an ordinary bank loan, card or merchant cash advance with all fees
No library item reviews a personal guarantee or lists the security a lender holds
No library item compares funding routes for a small firm: term loan, overdraft, asset finance, invoice finance or a government-backed loan
No library item does a quality of earnings review for a small private business; the add-back checker only tests one add-back against a cap
No library item runs a proof of cash test that ties reported sales to bank receipts
No library item scores sale readiness or plans an exit; searches for exit planning returned staff exit interviews
No library item explains or compares deal terms for a small business sale: earn-outs, seller loans, deferred payment or a letter of intent
No library item checks bank deposit protection limits or writes a simple cash policy for a small firm
No library item helps an owner choose how to pay themselves (salary, dividends, drawings) with questions for their accountant
No library item reviews a commercial property lease from the tenant's money side
No library item sets up a finance function: which accounting system, who does what, and a first set of controls
